text:
sasha: Heads-up: after yesterday's kernel mapping change I see a regression on small-chat workloads — p95 decode latency up ~2.2x on prod nodes. I ran a quick profiler and KV cache hit-rate drops during heavy interleaving of prefill+decode.
kevin: Ugh. Do you have the flamegraph or perf counters?
sasha: pasted a tiny snippet from flame: ```
# sample summarized
decode_stage  58%  (hot)
kernel_dispatch 22%
kv_lookup 12%
other 8%
```
sasha: Also saw this in the request tracer: when prefill and decode are mixed in the same batch we get lots of kernel switches and small fragmented kernels => higher launch overhead.
arin: Could be fragmentation of the batch into many kernel-codepaths. Might be our batching policy is letting prefill tokens piggyback on decode batches. We probably need stricter phase separation + token-budget thresholds.
kevin: I pulled metric history: p95 decode latency on region-us-east-1 at 2026-03-17T11:22: 210ms -> now ~470ms. KV cache occupancy dips right before the spike (we're evicting frequently).
maya: Noted. Any deploys around that window?
sasha: Kernel mapping roll 2345 at 11:10 — changed affinity so small models favor new fused-kernel. That mapping caused more kernel switches for long context streams.
build-bot: CI: benchmark-suite/split-batcher-compat failed on staging with 3 regressions (latency). Logs: /ci/bench/2345/log.txt
kevin: I think we need two changes: 1) stronger prefill/decode batch isolation (separate queues + dedicated batcher threads) 2) token_budget cap on mixed batches so prefill doesn't dominate.
arin: Agreed. Proposed quick experiment: create a "phase-tag" on requests (prefill|decode). In the scheduler, only merge same-phase requests unless both are tiny (<8 tokens). For mixed batches, enforce max-prefill-tokens fraction=0.2.
maya: Can we A/B that on a single pod-class first? Also watch KV hit-rate and context warmup time.
sasha: I'll prototype a scheduler toggle flag: "--phase_isolation=partial" that partitions queues and applies token caps. If it looks good we can flip it for all pod-classes.
kevin: Add metric booleans: batch.fragmentation_count, batch.kernel_switches_per_batch, kv.hit_rate_pre/post, decode.p95. We need dashboards.
arin: Also suggest a fallback mapping: if kernel_switches_per_batch > 1, prefer fallback_kernel with lower launch overhead even if slightly slower per-op. That reduces tail.
kevin: Good idea — cheaper launch wins tail-critical flows. We should simulate cost model: total_time = sum(launch + run*tokens) and pick kernel that minimizes total_time for observed batch composition.
sasha: Experimental config I want to test tonight on staging (pseudo):
```
scheduler:
  phase_isolation: partial
  small_merge_threshold: 8
  mixed_batch_prefill_token_fraction: 0.2
kernel_routing:
  fallback_policy: prefer_low_launch_if_switches>1
metrics:
  emit: [batch.fragmentation_count, kernel_switches_per_batch, kv.hit_rate]
```
kevin: Cool. I can wire up quick grafana panels. I'll also run synthetic traffic with varied token distributions to validate.
maya: Leave a roll-forward plan: if p95 improves by >20% and kv.hit_rate recovers, promote. If not, rollback. :+1:
sasha: One more note — we saw a KV drain window when batches with many prefill owners touched fresh contexts; add a short prefill KV warmup priority: when prefill wins a batch, mark context sticky for next 50ms to avoid immediate eviction churn.
arin: That's smart. Sticky marker TTL should be tunable. Could help reduce repeated cold KV lookups for streaming flows.
kevin: I'll add a synthetic scenario that emits many small stream continuations to stress the sticky logic.
build-bot: Deploy pipeline: branch "phase-isolation-experiment" queued to staging. Job link: https://ci.internal/2345
sasha: Thanks all — I'll push the scheduler toggle and config. We'll reconvene after one staged run and metrics lookgood.
kevin: Ping me if you want me to flip the rollout or run a canary against prod traffic slice.
maya: thx!
sasha: filing a short incident note in #incidents if we see continued tail regressions. For now schedule experiment and collect graphs.
